newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO urges Israel to halt settlement activity.
newsitem.headline: PLO urges Israel to halt settlement activity.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority sent Israel a letter on Monday urging it to halt immediately all settlement activity or risk "confrontation and disaster", a PLO peace negotiator said.

"A two-page letter was sent to Israeli negotiator Dan Shomron this morning, which urges the Israeli government to give peace a chance by immediately revoking plans and military orders to expand settlements and to halt all settlement activities," said negotiator Saeb Erekat.

"The letter expressed the Palestinian Authority's deep concern vis-a-vis the Israeli government's policy of settlement expansion in the West Bank, including Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip," he told Reuters.
Erekat, who sent the letter to Shomron, said the message warned that "continuation of such policies will bring both of our peoples back to the square of confrontation and disaster".
He cited plans approved by Israel to add thousands of housing units in parts of the West Bank and orders to confiscate more Palestinian land.
These plans, Erekat said, "constitute not only a flagrant violation of the agreement signed, but also a serious threat that will bury the hope of peace".

Under the 1993 PLO-Israel peace deal, Israel has handed over parts of the West Bank and Gaza to Palestinian self-rule but the fate of settlements has been left to "final-status" talks that have been suspended since Israel's right-wing new Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took office in June.

"The interim accord also states that neither side shall initiate or take any step that will change the status of Palestinian territories or the issues of final status, such as Jerusalem and settlements," Erekat said.
Netanyahu enraged Palestinians when he lifted a four-year freeze on Jewish settlement construction after he took office.
He has approved the construction of thousands of new homes for Jews in existing settlements in the West Bank since August but has yet to give permission for any additional communities to be built.
Some 130,000 Jews live in settlements scattered among the more than two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.

PLO officials use words such as "cancerous" to describe settlements. President Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority formed committees on Friday to formulate a strategy for battling Netanyahu's settlement policies.
